title: Anatomy of a License Statement
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Educational Resources
description: Find the seven parts of a complete license statement on a drawing of a lesson page footer, then identify each part from a description of how it looks.

learningObjectives: The learner will identify the seven parts of a complete license statement on an annotated page footer from a description of each part, with at least 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt.
prerequisites: The terms license statement, license name and version, and third-party content

dependencies: None. The drawing is inline SVG and the script is plain JavaScript.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then quiz on the same picture
keyQuestions: Which part of the footer tells readers the license version?
Which part can a reader not see?
commonMisconceptions: The license icons alone are the license
"CC BY" without a version is a complete statement
A license statement on a page covers every image on it
assessmentOpportunities: Why is "CC BY" with no version an incomplete statement?
Do the license icons alone make a license statement?
Does a license statement on a page cover every image on it?
Where can a reader find the machine-readable marking?

controls.name: Explore and Quiz me buttons
controls.description: switch modes. Quiz me starts a new run.
